title: The New Code — Sean Grove, OpenAI
talk_summary: Sean Grove argues that the durable artifact in software work is the written specification of intent, not the generated code, because code is a lossy projection of intent and prompts are currently thrown away while binaries are versioned. He proposes treating specs as executable, testable, composable code with clause IDs, embedded eval prompts, and linting for ambiguity, and aligning models to them via deliberative alignment scoring.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before generating code, write a durable spec capturing intent, values, and success criteria, and keep it as the versioned source artifact rather than discarding the prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We keep the generated code and we delete the prompt... like you shred the source and then you very carefully version control the binary.

takeaways.technique: Clause IDs with embedded adversarial test prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Give every clause in the spec an ID and store one or more challenging prompts per clause in a sibling file, so the spec encodes its own success criteria and can be graded.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every clause in the model spec has an ID here... that contains one or more challenging prompts for this exact clause.

takeaways.technique: Spec as both eval and training material (deliberative alignment loop)
takeaways.what_they_do: Sample model responses to challenging prompts, have a stronger model score each response against the spec, and use the scores to reinforce or select behavior.

takeaways.technique: Spec linting for ambiguity and cross-spec consistency checks
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat specs like typed code: lint for ambiguous language and detect conflicts between specs owned by different teams, blocking publication on conflict.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if department A writes a spec and department B writes a spec and there is a conflict in there you want to be able to pull that forward and maybe block the publication

takeaways.technique: Push stable policy into persistent context, not per-run prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than re-injecting the spec in every sample (which detracts from compute), move stable policy into weights or persistent system/developer messages so it is applied as muscle memory.
